listenings.text: I am Ayse Demir, from Istanbul. Last year I went to a pain congress in Lisbon and it changed the way I work. I presented a poster on the second day. Nobody came for the first twenty minutes and I felt terrible. Then one professor stopped, asked me three questions, and stayed for half an hour. His feedback was hard, but he was right, and I changed my method because of it. The keynote on Friday was excellent, but honestly, the poster session was the part that mattered. I did not talk to many people that week. I talked to four, and two of them are now my co-authors.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome back. A short summary of yesterday, for the people who arrived this morning. The opening keynote was given by Professor Andersen and it was about pain in low income countries. After lunch we had three parallel sessions, and the room for the session on nerve damage was too small, so we moved it to the main hall. The poster session ran from four to six and there were ninety-one posters. Today the programme starts at nine in this room. Please note that the venue for the closing dinner changed. It is not the hotel. It is the university club, and the buses leave at seven.
